about: The questions a rule may ask of a model in place of a list of words (judgements.mjs). Each kind is one question about one subject: `asks` is the question, `subject` what it is asked of, `verdicts` the answers it takes with what each means, `quoteFor` the verdicts whose answer quotes the words of the subject they rest on, and `fields` what an answer carries beside its verdict. A recorded answer is replayed under a key of the kind, its `version`, the subject and the context: raise the version when the question's meaning changes, and every subject is asked again. A kind marked `spine` reads what the storyline critique is bound to: the critique waits until its questions are answered.

column-judges.asks: Does this table column give a judgement on each row - who leads or wins, a verdict, a rating, a status, how confident the call is - rather than another fact about the row?
column-judges.subject: the column's header and the words in its cells; the context is the table's other headers

verdicts.judges: the cells are judgements on the rows
verdicts.states-facts: the cells are facts, descriptions or evidence, not a judgement

prose-alternatives.asks: Are these paragraphs alternatives the reader is asked to compare - scenarios, options, paths, cases, futures - rather than the steps of one argument?
prose-alternatives.subject: the page's title and purpose, and each paragraph with its lead

verdicts.alternatives: each paragraph sets out one alternative to be weighed against the others
verdicts.one-argument: the paragraphs build one argument, or are not alternatives

row-is-total.asks: Is this table row a total - a sum, a grand total, an overall figure for the rows above it - rather than a group heading or a row of its own?
row-is-total.subject: the row's label; the context is the table's headers and the labels of the rows around it

verdicts.total: the row closes the table as a total of the rows
verdicts.not-total: the row heads a group, or is a row of its own

axis-measures-time.asks: Does this chart axis measure time - dates, years, months, time elapsed since an event?
axis-measures-time.subject: the axis label

verdicts.time: the axis is a time scale
verdicts.not-time: the axis measures something other than time

header-concludes.asks: Does this table column header name an inference drawn from the row - what it means, implies, recommends or decides - rather than one more fact about the row?
header-concludes.subject: the column's header; the context is the table's other headers

verdicts.concludes: the header names what follows from the row
verdicts.names-a-fact: the header names a fact or measure about the row

pill-states-status.asks: Does the text of this status pill state a status or verdict that a status colour can carry (on track, at risk, leads, behind), rather than say there is no verdict (split, mixed, unranked, not comparable, too early, not disclosed)?
pill-states-status.subject: the pill's text; the context is the colour it is drawn in

verdicts.status: the text states a status or verdict
verdicts.no-verdict: the text says there is no verdict to colour

heading-says-snapshots.asks: Does this chart heading or unit tell the reader that its columns are separate snapshots at chosen dates rather than an evenly spaced series?
heading-says-snapshots.subject: the chart's heading and unit; the context is its categories

verdicts.says-snapshots: the reader is told the columns are chosen dates
verdicts.reads-as-series: nothing tells the reader the gaps between the columns differ

tiles-one-measure.asks: Do two of these figure tiles give one measure at two dates, or for two members, so that the reader compares them across the boxes?
tiles-one-measure.subject: the tiles, each an id with its figure and label; the context is the players the deck names

verdicts.one-measure: two tiles are one measure at two dates or for two members
verdicts.different-measures: every tile gives a different measure

pair.about: the ids of the two tiles that give one measure

title-leads-with-gap.asks: Does this slide title lead with a gap in the evidence - what it lacks, cannot settle, leaves undisclosed or unproven, or that the call is split - rather than with a finding?
title-leads-with-gap.subject: the title

verdicts.gap: the title's main statement is what the evidence cannot show
verdicts.finding: the title states a finding, whatever limit it also names

title-count-only.asks: Does this slide title only state how many or how much - a count or measurement with no comparator (against a peer, a target, a prior period) and no consequence?
title-count-only.subject: the title

verdicts.count-only: the title states a measurement and nothing it is against or what follows
verdicts.compares: the title says what the number is against, or what follows from it

heading-states-result.asks: Does this chart heading or unit state a result the chart shows - a value, a change, a share, a rank reached - rather than only name the measure, its population, its period or its scale?
heading-states-result.subject: the heading or unit text, and which of the two it is

verdicts.result: the text states a value or change the chart's marks show
verdicts.describes: the text names the measure, population, period, sample, set or scale

qualification-says-approximate.asks: Does this qualification tell the reader that the interval's figures are approximate readings rather than exact source values?
qualification-says-approximate.subject: the qualification text

verdicts.approximate: the reader is told the figures are approximate
verdicts.unqualified: the text does not say the figures are approximate

answer-contradicted.asks: Does the deck's answer recommend one thing without condition, while one or more pages recommend something else that the answer does not admit?
answer-contradicted.subject: the deck's answer, and each page's claim with its id

verdicts.contradicted: a page recommends what the unconditional answer rules out
verdicts.consistent: the pages' recommendations agree with the answer, or the answer names the condition under which each holds, or the answer recommends nothing

pages.about: the ids of the pages whose claims recommend what the answer rules out

source-cites-pointer.asks: Does this source line or note cite an internal code or pointer the reader cannot look up - a ledger entry, a register reference, a code such as 'S3+S7' - instead of naming the source?
source-cites-pointer.subject: the source line or note

verdicts.pointer: the line points at a code or ledger the reader does not have
verdicts.names-source: the line names its sources, or is a note that cites nothing

planning-label.asks: Does this line of a slide open with a planning label - a word that names the kind of sentence it is (Interpretation, Takeaway, Insight, So what, Caveat, Note that) - rather than with its content?
planning-label.subject: the line

verdicts.planning-label: the line opens by labelling itself
verdicts.content: the line's opening words are content

commentary-caveats.asks: Which of these lines of a slide's commentary state what the evidence does not show, settle or establish, rather than a finding? A finding in contrastive form ('X does not decide the city; it decides the neighbourhood') is a finding.
commentary-caveats.subject: the commentary lines, each with its id

verdicts.some-caveats: one or more lines are caveats

caveats.about: the ids of the lines that are caveats

shares-in-words.asks: Which shares do these lines state in words rather than as a percentage - 'half', 'two thirds', 'one in four', 'most'? Give each with the fraction it states; leave out shares written as a percentage and words that state no definite share.
shares-in-words.subject: the lines of the slide, each with its id

verdicts.states-shares: one or more lines state a definite share in words
verdicts.no-shares: no line states a definite share in words

shares.about: each share as { "phrase": the words, copied exactly, "share": the fraction from 0 to 1 }

title-count-check.asks: The title counts something ('three of four ...'). Counting it off these labels the page draws, does the page show the count the title states?
title-count-check.subject: the title and the labels of the set the title counts across

verdicts.agrees: the labels show the count the title states, or they are not what the title counts
verdicts.disagrees: the labels show a different count

counted.about: how many of the labels carry what the title counts
